transcript.text: Samsung RS68A8820S9/EU flashing 22E on the display and the fridge side isn't as cold as it should be. What does 22E mean and can I fix it?

1. Ice build-up has jammed the fan or blocked the air path — often due to a defrost fault.
2. The fan motor or its wiring/control has failed.
3. You may be able to deal with an ice blockage, but a failed fan motor or its electrical supply normally needs an engineer. 1. Check the fridge setting is around 3–5°C, freezer -18°C, with no Holiday/Eco mode selected. This rules out a setting issue.
2. Make sure food is not pressed against the vents at the back/top of the fridge or packed tightly around freezer air outlets. If airflow returns after moving items, leave space around the vents.
3. With the freezer door open, press and hold the door switch by hand for a few seconds. Listen for a fan whirr. Also look for a thick sheet of frost or ice on the rear panel inside the freezer. Do not remove panels while it is powered. If the fan is audible but there is heavy ice or little air into the fridge, the likely underlying fault is the defrost system rather than the fan itself. A full switch-off and unplugged defrost for 24–48 hours, with towels down and both doors open, can temporarily restore cooling; if 22E returns, it needs diagnosis of the defrost components. If the freezer is cold, there is no heavy ice, and the fan stays silent with the door switch held in, the evaporator fan or its control circuit is the likely fault and an engineer is the sensible route.

Fridge reads 9C and the airflow from the vents is very weak. There's a bit of frost around the vent at the top back of the fridge, but I haven't checked the freezer rear panel. I'm not sure what the Eco/Holiday settings are set to, and I haven't tried the door switch fan test yet. No burning smell or tripping, by the way. Should I do the full defrost?

Yes — a full manual defrost is a sensible next step if the quick fan check suggests ice is restricting it. Code 22E is used for a fridge evaporator-fan fault: the fan may be unable to turn because of ice, or the fan/motor circuit may not be detected running. With 9°C in the fridge, weak vent airflow and frost at a vent, an ice-related airflow blockage is currently the leading possibility. Before committing to the defrost, do these two quick checks: 1. Check the settings: set the fridge to 3–5°C and freezer to -18°C, and make sure Holiday/Eco is not selected. A mode or incorrect setting can reduce cooling, though it would not usually explain 22E. 2. Open the freezer and press/hold its door switch for a few seconds. Listen for a fan whirr. Keep hands clear of any vents. - Fan running, but fridge airflow remains weak: that strongly favours ice blocking the air path/defrost system. - No fan sound: it could be jammed in ice, or the fan motor/control circuit has failed. If you proceed, switch it off at the socket and unplug it, move food to cool bags or another freezer, put towels down, and leave both doors open for 24–48 hours so all hidden ice melts. Do not chip ice with a knife or use a hairdryer. Dry it thoroughly before restarting. If it cools normally after defrosting but 22E or weak airflow returns over the following days, the automatic defrost system needs an engineer diagnosis. If the fan remains silent and 22E returns immediately after a complete defrost, a fridge evaporator fan or its wiring/control is more likely and is also an engineer repair.

I tried the freezer door switch but I can't tell whether I'm hearing the fan or just the normal fridge noise. I'll go ahead with the full defrost. I've got a cool box for the food. Anything else I should do before I switch it off?

Yes. Before switching off, take a quick photo of the 22E display, remove loose food and the ice bin, and place plenty of towels around the base—there can be more meltwater than expected. Leave both doors held open, rather than repeatedly opening them, and keep pets/children away from the water. Once all ice has melted, wipe the compartments dry. If you can see a fridge drain channel/hole, flush it gently with a little warm water or clear it only with something soft; do not use anything sharp. Do not chip at ice or use a hairdryer/heat gun. 22E is consistent with the fridge evaporator fan not being detected running. In your case, weak airflow and frost make ice stopping the fan or air path the leading possibility; the defrost will distinguish that from a failed fan/circuit. After restarting, allow roughly 24 hours with the doors mostly shut. If cooling and airflow recover but 22E returns after days or weeks, the automatic defrost system needs an engineer diagnosis. If 22E returns straight away or airflow remains weak after a complete defrost, the fan motor or its wiring/control is more likely and an engineer is the sensible next step.
Great, thanks. I'll take a photo of the display, empty it out and get the towels down before switching it off. If 22E comes back after the defrost, who should I contact?

If 22E returns after a complete defrost, contact Samsung’s authorised appliance service/repair team first, quoting the full model RS68A8820S9/EU and the flashing 22E code. If it is still within the retailer or manufacturer warranty period, use the retailer/Samsung warranty route rather than booking an independent repairer. 22E is associated with the fridge evaporator fan not being detected running. In this situation it can be caused by ice preventing airflow or jamming the fan, but if it returns after a proper defrost it is more likely to need an engineer to diagnose the automatic defrost system or the fan motor/wiring/control circuit. Those are internal repairs rather than a sensible DIY part swap. When booking, tell them: “Fridge section is warming, airflow was weak, there was frost around the upper rear vent, and 22E returned after a 24–48 hour manual defrost” — if that is what happens. That should help them attend prepared to investigate the evaporator fan and defrost circuit. After the defrost and restart, allow around 24 hours for temperatures and airflow to settle before judging the result.

Less commonly, the fridge vents are blocked by food or a temperature/mode setting is wrong.
